body: St. Louis Public Radio reported on Sept. 17, 2026 that the developer behind a planned $3.1 billion data center in Midtown St. Louis had sued the city that week. TerraWatt plans a 120-megawatt data center in the old Famous-Barr warehouse on Market Street, near the Armory, as part of a planned technology district. The petition, filed by TerraWatt partner David Lambiaso against the city's Board of Adjustment, challenges two conditions the board attached to the project's conditional use permit.

The first condition requires the data center to use 2.4 megawatts of renewable energy, which the complaint calls "practically impossible on the 11-acre site." The second requires the Board of Aldermen to approve a community benefits agreement. The suit alleges both requirements "exceed the scope of authority" of the board and asks that they be struck from the permit. According to the station, the city's Land Clearance for Redevelopment Authority approved the community benefits agreement the same week. Mayor Cara Spencer did not immediately respond to the station's request for comment.

The board had voted unanimously on July 29, 2026 to let the permit proceed with amendments after more than 11 hours of public comment, St. Louis Public Radio reported; its changes included barring backup generator testing on bad air quality days and requiring a small amount of on-site renewable energy generation. On Aug. 28, a group of opponents that includes the Missouri Coalition for the Environment sued the city, arguing the board "erred in deciding to deny the appeals and grant" the permit and acted "contrary to law." That suit also names Lambiaso. The opponents asked the court for a stay while the case proceeds and for reversal of the board's decision; a spokeswoman for the mayor said the city does not comment on pending legal matters.

Consultants working for TerraWatt estimate the project would generate about $445 million in tax revenue over 10 years for the city, St. Louis Public Schools and other local taxing authorities, according to the station.

timeline.label: Board of Adjustment votes unanimously to let the data center's conditional use permit proceed with amendments
Missouri Coalition for the Environment and other opponents sue the city, arguing the permit was illegally granted
A TerraWatt partner sues the Board of Adjustment to strike two conditions from the permit
